subject: TTFT + streaming SLO follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeretail.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: TTFT + streaming SLO follow-up

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the perf targets captured and can validate feasibility with infra/serving: 

What we heard (your asks):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) target: <= 250 ms P95 for the average user request (targeting the search/assistant path).
- Streaming delivery: SSE preferred (WebSocket ok); chunk cadence: first chunk within TTFT, subsequent chunks at ~100-200 ms cadence (aim for ~150 ms typical).
- Concurrency/throughput: expected baseline 20 req/s with spikes to 80–100 concurrent streaming sessions during peak promotions.
- Payloads: typical prompt size ~120 tokens, responses ~600 tokens; some long responses up to 2k tokens for summaries.
- Success criteria: <250 ms P95 TTFT, sustained stream cadence under 200 ms between chunks, and no dropped connections during 95th-percentile load.

Requested materials (I've attached):
- Our mutual action plan (redwood-map-ttft.pdf)
- Your anonymized traffic sample (acme-traffic-sample.csv) — thanks for sharing.

Ask / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the concurrency spike pattern (80–100) and whether the 20 req/s baseline is per region or global?
2) We'll run an internal perf validation and propose one of two implementation options (SSE with HTTP/2 keepalives or WebSocket pinned connections) plus a measurement plan. Expect a follow-up by EOD tomorrow with a recommended configuration and a short test plan.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Vivek (serving lead) and your infra folks — options: Wed 12/3 10–11am PT or Thu 12/4 9–10am PT.

If you want anything changed in the MAP or the targets above, flag it and we'll iterate.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-map-ttft.pdf, acme-traffic-sample.csv

Thanks Marissa — this aligns with what we discussed. Two clarifications from our side: 
1) The 20 req/s baseline is global, but our primary US region will see ~70% of traffic at peak.
2) For chunk cadence, we care more about perceivable progress — first chunk within the TTFT, and then steady chunks every ~150ms is ideal. We prefer SSE for browser clients, WebSocket for mobile where we have lower TLS setup costs.

We can do Wed 12/3 10am PT for the tech deep-dive — I'll invite our infra lead (will add to thread).

Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeretail.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT + streaming SLO follow-up

Appreciate the confirmation, Jordan — Wed 12/3 10am PT is on our side. I added Vivek and Rishi to help validate the perf/readiness side. Two quick notes from our end before the call so your infra lead has context: 

Redwood proposed approaches (we'll validate and bring numbers on Wed):
A) SSE (HTTP/2) single-shot streaming: low-management on client, works well with browser clients. Expected TTFT range (for typical model ensembles): 120–260 ms P95 depending on model size and quantization. Chunk cadence after first token: typically 80–180 ms depending on response generation rate and batching.
B) WebSocket pinned connection: lower per-message overhead for mobile, slightly better tail latency for steady low-latency chunks at high concurrency. Expected TTFT range: 110–230 ms P95.

Measurement plan we'll propose:
- Synthetic perf runs using your sample traffic profile (we'll replay prompt lengths and concurrency spikes).
- Measure: TTFT P50/P95/P99, chunk inter-arrival distribution (ms), connection drop rate, token throughput (tokens/sec) per worker.
- Canary test plan: small percent of production traffic routed to dedicated pool + telemetry hooks (span-level TTFT) and automated alerting if P95 > target or chunk cadence degradation observed.

Open question for your infra lead: do you have strict connection timeouts for long-lived SSE/WebSocket connections (e.g., proxies/load balancers that enforce 60s idle timeouts)? If so, we'll need to account for keepalive strategies.

I'll send a short perf-run proposal and timeline by EOD today (Tue) and a calendar invite for Wed.

Thanks,
Marissa

Quick feasibility note — internal only: 
- Based on the sample and the targets (<=250ms P95 TTFT, 100 concurrent streams), we should be able to meet goals with a dedicated pool using 8xA100-equivalents (quantized 4-bit where possible) plus KV-prefetching for common prompts. We'll run a focused perf replay tonight to get concrete P95 numbers across model variants (base vs. tuned).
- For chunk cadence consistency, prioritize lower-latency kernels + fewer cross-device fetches; that will keep inter-chunk jitter under 150ms in most cases.
- Keepalive: we recommend 30s HTTP/2 pings for SSE paths to survive intermediate proxies.

I'll surface the concrete numbers in the Wed deep-dive; if Rishi or Marissa want anything added to the perf plan before the analytic runs, call it out.

— Vivek
Serving Lead | Redwood Inference
